tasks.short: Warn rule violators and handle necessary interventions

steps.what: Assess observed rule infractions and clarify the situation with those involved
Warn persons of violations and seek voluntary compliance or authorised assistance
Handle necessary apprehension or eviction within training and applicable authority

tasks.design: Keep assessment, warnings and any necessary intervention with trained guards under current site procedures. No automated suspicion score, force recommendation or software-triggered removal is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on uncertain live events and accountable physical intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software mechanism justifies reducing this direct work.
tasks.still_hard: Assess context and resolve conflict proportionately.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, de-escalate and recognise the limits of authority.
tasks.altitude: The guard retains existing responsibilities and limits.

reach.learn: Explain observed facts and escalation choices

evidence.claim: Live warnings and physical interventions require contextual human judgement and cannot be replaced by record automation.

assumptions: No additional intervention powers are assumed. Current training and site procedures govern conduct.
Shares are provisional averages across the full task, not a prescribed sequence requiring every incident to end in apprehension.
Observation and clarification time remain in s1; no structured violation label is supplied for free. Incident report production is outside this boundary.
No new system is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which intervention and escalation authority the guard actually has
research_questions: Do current procedures clearly distinguish observed facts from assumptions when reviewing interventions?

incremental.description: No additional intervention technology or process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+45+20=100. No observation, dialogue or intervention time changes, and no hypothetical incident reduction is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer after-hours calls and take messages

steps.what: Answer telephone calls and establish the caller’s question or message
Find approved public information or the correct after-hours contact
Answer questions, provide permitted information and record or relay messages

tasks.design: Configure a searchable, approved after-hours directory in {DOCS} with public answers and escalation contacts. The guard interprets calls, reads the relevant entry and decides what may be disclosed; no generated voice agent answers callers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding a current answer or contact across documents interrupts calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and a maintained directory can simplify retrieval without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Distress, ambiguous requests and requests for restricted information.
tasks.human_edge: Listen carefully and recognise when a call needs escalation.
tasks.altitude: The guard finds approved information faster, with unchanged disclosure and escalation rights.

reach.task: Maintain public answers and routing guidance
reach.learn: Separate public information from restricted operational details

evidence.claim: A searchable approved directory can reduce manual information lookup; no digest source demonstrates this guard-call use case.

assumptions: Reception or site administration produces answer_topic, approved_text, contact_route, owner and review_date by checking existing instructions. Initial capture belongs in the rollout estimate and recurring checking is counted as other-role upkeep.
Guard determines the request in s1 and checks relevance and currency in s2; no free classified caller-intent feed is assumed.
Missing or expired entries lead to the existing manual escalation route. Test current document search first; restrict the directory to approved information.
Message capture and caller interaction retain their full time in s3.
unknowns: Whether an approved directory already exists
Who owns its accuracy and which information may be disclosed
research_questions: Does indexed lookup reduce call time after relevance checking and directory upkeep are included?

already_counted.description: Read and verify the retrieved directory entry

incremental.description: Flag expired entries and routing failures
Verify and update answers and contact routes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=30+9+55=94; gross=6%; minus 1 focal upkeep gives 5% net. Low: present directory is already effective. High: lookup alone shortens; listening, answering, message capture and escalation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Recognise an emergency and establish observed facts and location
Call police or fire departments and answer the dispatcher’s questions

tasks.design: Retain direct emergency calling through {TELEPHONY} using current emergency procedures and site-location guidance. Do not insert a model, form-completion prerequisite or new approval before contacting the dispatcher.
tasks.previous_blocker: The communication is urgent, situational and potentially life-critical.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing telephone and emergency procedures remain the appropriate mechanism.
tasks.still_hard: Communicate uncertain facts accurately while conditions change.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise urgency and respond to the dispatcher’s questions.
tasks.altitude: Emergency escalation authority and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Locate site instructions and communicate observed facts

evidence.claim: Emergency requests rely on live observation and dispatcher dialogue; automation is not established for this task by the digest.

assumptions: The guard establishes location and facts in s1; no prevalidated structured emergency payload is assumed and uncertain details are communicated as uncertain.
Site administration supplies existing location guidance; its upkeep is unchanged. No automated dispatch interface is introduced.
No new system means zero incremental maintenance; subsequent physical response and incident reporting are outside this call task.
unknowns: Which current site instructions and communication equipment apply
research_questions: Can guards locate current site-location guidance during a practice exercise?

incremental.description: No additional emergency-calling technology or workflow

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+65=100. Recognition, fact gathering and emergency dialogue remain unchanged; no reduced emergency response time is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Guards can retrieve approved after-hours information more easily while retaining live intervention and emergency escalation responsibilities.
reach: Work with reception on accurate public information
role.ambitious_version: Reduce routine lookup interruptions while preserving direct human judgement in consequential situations.
